text:
Aisha: Quick sync — we need clear acceptance criteria for BYOK handshake onboarding. Customers repeatedly ask for evidence export + retention guarantees. What do we consider MUST-have for MVP vs nice-to-have post-launch? cc @Priya :eyes:
Marco: For MVP I think MUSTs are: KMS URI support, signed handshake tokens, audit events for each handshake step, and a documented API contract. Nice-to-have: automated escrow flow, per-tenant retention UI.
Priya: +1. Add SOC2-specific items as MUST: key rotation policy doc, proof-of-possession sample, and an immutable audit trail for key usage. Legal needs to sign off on escrow language before we promise it.
Sam: Ops perspective — we need an end-to-end test harness that can simulate: rotate key, handshake, evidence export, and legal-hold restore. Also a CLI for ops to trigger evidence exports (signed) for customers.
Eve: From a customer POV: the handshake must be auditable. We need a standardized evidence package format and a clear SLA for export (eg 48h for export deliverable). Also: legal-hold toggle that pauses retention deletion.
Aisha: Draft acceptance criteria attempt below — please react with :thumbsup: if OK or list edits.
Aisha: MVP acceptance criteria (must):
- API: POST /byok/handshake v1 with documented request/response schema.
- Security: handshake requests must be signed by customer (ECDSA) and validated server-side.
- Audit: every handshake and subsequent key-usage event emits an immutable audit event (request_id + actor + outcome).
- Evidence export: produce a signed evidence package (manifest + logs) within 72h of request.
- Retention: support configurable retention windows per tenant (min 0d, default 90d).
- Legal hold: ability to apply a legal hold flag via API that prevents deletions.
Aisha: Post-launch (nice-to-have / v2):
- Automated KMS escrow workflow + escrow attestation.
- Per-tenant retention UI in Console and export history.
- SLA tiers: 48h priority export, 72h standard.
Marco: Implementation notes: audit events should look like: `audit.event("byok.handshake", {request_id, customer_id, key_uri, status})`. Keep payload small. We should reuse existing trace IDs so it ties into Console traces.
Priya: For SOC2 evidence, the exported package must contain: chain-of-custody manifest, signed handshake payload, key metadata (no secret material), and raw audit log slice. We should provide a sample package for legal review.
Sam: Ops runbook items (MVP): steps to validate a failed handshake, how to regenerate evidence, emergency revoke flow. We should add these as acceptance tests in CI.
Aisha: Small API example to include in the spec: 
```json
{
  "customer_id": "cust-123",
  "key_uri": "kms://redwood-proj/key-abc",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-21T15:12:00Z",
  "signature": "BASE64_SIG"
}
```
Aisha: Open questions: 1) retention default (90d vs 180d)? 2) export SLA for large tenants (>1TB logs) — do we provide streaming exports or bucket access? 3) Who owns legal-hold UI copy?
Eve: Default 90d is fine for most, but enterprise customers will want 180d or custom. For big tenants we must offer S3 deliverable + manifest; streaming can be post-launch.
Priya: Legal-hold copy: Legal + Product should own it. I'll loop in Legal. Also, for rotation proof we need a signed rotation event in the audit trail.
Marco: Tech note: we should implement automatic sampling retention for very large volumes to keep export sizes reasonable; include sampling metadata in manifest. That can be opt-in.
Aisha: Next steps: Priya to confirm SOC2 evidence fields by EOD Fri; Sam to draft ops runbook checklist; Marco to stub API spec and wireframe minimal Console controls; I'll compile an RFC once we have those. cc @deploy-bot
deploy-bot: New RFC created: /rfc/byok-handshake-onboarding (draft) — please review
Sam: I'll have a first ops checklist PR by Tuesday.
Priya: Legal looped in (added to thread).
Eve: Thanks — I'll validate export format with our compliance team and send feedback next week.
Aisha: Great — thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the RFC comments. :rocket:
